name: SWE-bench Verified
description: A human-validated subset of 500 real GitHub-issue instances from SWE-bench. Models must produce a patch that passes the repo's unit tests. These scores are from the bash-only leaderboard (mini-SWE-agent v2.0.0 scaffold), which standardises the harness so the model weights are the primary variable. Metric: % of instances resolved.

name: Aider Polyglot
description: 225 Exercism coding exercises across C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python and Rust. The model must read the spec and existing files, edit them to pass the unit tests, and express its edits in Aider's diff format. Reported metric is Pass rate 2 (% of tests passing after up to two attempts).

name: Humanity's Last Exam
description: 2,500 graduate-level, subject-diverse questions from nearly 1,000 expert contributors, spanning mathematics, humanities, and natural sciences. Designed so that frontier LLMs still score far below expert humans. Score is % accuracy on the public set.

name: GPQA Diamond
description: 198 multiple-choice PhD-level science questions (biology, chemistry, physics) where domain experts answer correctly but non-experts, even with unrestricted Google access, typically cannot. Random baseline is 25%. Scores here are from Epoch AI's independent re-evaluations.

name: FrontierMath
description: A hidden set of hundreds of original, expert-level mathematics problems crafted and vetted by professional mathematicians, spanning undergraduate through research-level mathematics. Models get a Python tool and must submit a callable answer. Solutions are graded by exact-match to a rubric. Score is % correct (over Tiers 1-3 unless noted).

name: SimpleBench
description: 200+ multiple-choice "trick" questions that require common-sense reasoning, spatio-temporal reasoning, and linguistic-adversarial robustness. Non-specialist humans score ~84% baseline; frontier LLMs still lag. Score is averaged accuracy (AVG@5) in MCQ mode.

name: OTIS Mock AIME 2024-2025
description: 45 integer-answer problems drawn from the unofficial OTIS Mock AIME exams (2024 & 2025), written by Olympiad Training for Individual Study participants. Harder than MATH-Level-5 but easier than FrontierMath; answers are integers 0-999. Scores from Epoch AI's independent evaluation.

name: MATH Level 5
description: The 1,324 hardest problems from Hendrycks et al.'s MATH dataset (competition math from AMC/AIME etc.). Scored via a combination of normalised string match, symbolic equivalence, and model-graded equivalence. Scores here are Epoch AI's independent evaluations.

name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
description: Agents use a real bash terminal to complete tasks: editing files, running commands, debugging code. Each submission pairs a model with a scaffold (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Terminus 2, Goose, ForgeCode, ...). We record the best agent-model combination per model. Score is % tasks completed over repeated runs.

name: WeirdML v2
description: Models write PyTorch code to train ML models on non-standard tasks (shape recognition, digit classification, chess outcome prediction, …). Each task is run ≥15 times in an isolated Docker/GPU sandbox; each run gets up to 5 iterations with execution feedback. Score is mean best-accuracy per task, averaged across tasks.

name: BALROG
description: A suite of text-based games of varying difficulty (e.g. Hades, Keplar, NetHack-style). Scores are the percentage of games completed successfully, averaged across repeated runs.

name: Fiction.liveBench
description: Tests long-context comprehension: models answer recall questions about long serialised stories hosted on Fiction.live. Questions probe events, characters, and chronological order across the full story context. Score is % correct.

name: WebDev Arena
description: Bradley-Terry ELO-style leaderboard where two models each build a website for the same prompt and human voters rate which is better on aesthetics and function. Score is the resulting rating (higher is better).

name: VPCT (Visual Physics Comprehension Test)
description: Each problem shows an image of a ramp with buckets; the model must predict into which bucket a ball will land. Probes basic multimodal understanding of gravity, trajectory, and geometry.

name: GeoBench
description: GeoGuessr-style multimodal benchmark: given 100 street-level photos (sampled from five community maps), models must guess the country and lat/long coordinates. Score combines geographic distance with country accuracy (higher is better; practical range 0-5000).

name: Factorio Learning Environment
description: Agents control Factorio to build factories across lab-play tasks (e.g. craft 100 transport belts) and open-play factory construction. Score is a composite game-progress metric (higher is better; typical range 0-50).

name: ARC-AGI-1
description: ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) v1, semi-private evaluation set. Each task is a set of input→output grid pairs; the model must infer the transformation rule from 2-3 demos and apply it to a test input. Measures abstract/fluid reasoning. Score is the fraction solved (random baseline ~0).

name: ARC-AGI-2
description: The 2024/25 successor to ARC-AGI, harder and still targeting abstract reasoning the way v1 did — but with tasks specifically selected to resist the test-time-search tricks that saturated v1. Semi-private eval, score is fraction solved.
